intermediate_mechanisms: How loss of transduction leads to hair-cell death in TOMT deficiency has not been studied. In mouse, transduction is lost while other outer hair cell properties are still normal, and degeneration follows the same time course as in TMC-null mice, but no death pathway has been described.

nodes.description: Without TMC1 and TMC2 in the stereocilia, cochlear hair cells cannot convert hair-bundle deflection into a transduction current. In Tomt add/add mice, outer hair cell transducer currents are already very small at postnatal day 4 and absent by day 7, while membrane potential, outward currents and nonlinear capacitance are normal, so the defect is specific to transduction rather than a sign of a sick cell. Zebrafish tomt mutants lack transduction in both auditory and vestibular hair cells. This is the node at which the disease specializes the hair-cell mechanotransduction failure of the sensorineural hair cell loss module.

nodes.description: Mice homozygous for the Tomt add missense allele show progressive degeneration of the organ of Corti. This follows the loss of transduction, but the steps in between are not known, and the human course is undocumented: no temporal bone from a DFNB63 patient has been studied, and the human hearing loss is usually described as congenital and profound rather than progressive.

nodes.description: Cochlear implantation is used for the profound loss typical of DFNB63. The lesion is in the hair cell, so the auditory nerve that an implant stimulates is not the primary target of the disease. Outcome data are anecdotal: in the Mauritanian report, early implantation appeared to improve hearing in one carrier of the p.Leu60Pro genotype. No series of DFNB63 implant outcomes has been published.

nodes.description: TOMT is enriched in the Golgi apparatus of hair cells and is itself excluded from the hair bundle. It binds TMC1 and TMC2, the pore-forming subunits of the mechanoelectrical transduction channel, and is needed to move them through the secretory pathway to the stereocilia. Without TOMT, TMC1 and TMC2 fail to reach the bundle, whereas other MET complex proteins still do. The interaction with TMC1 is modulated by His183 in the putative active site of TOMT, but the methyltransferase activity itself is not required. Evidence is from zebrafish and mouse hair cells and from HEK293 co-expression.

nodes.description: Hearing aids are an option where residual hearing allows useful benefit, most plausibly at the milder, high-frequency end of the spectrum. No DFNB63-specific outcome data exist: the only cited source is a ski-slope hearing loss series in which LRTOMT was one of several causal genes, and it does not report hearing-aid use by gene.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous LRTOMT variants remove or impair the LRTOMT2 (TOMT) product. The reported alleles include splice-site, frameshift and missense changes; the missense alleles of the discovery report lie in the methyltransferase-like domain and are predicted to destabilize it. TOMT is expressed in the sensory hair cells of the cochlea and vestibular organs. This is the initiating lesion and the node at which the disease specializes the generic cochlear sensory-epithelium insult of the sensorineural hair cell loss module.
